# CloudWatch metric filters and queries

**Status**: written without AWS access. The `aws/spans` log group is generated by CloudWatch, not by
our exporter, so every JSON path below is a **validation item** for the first AWS run (quickstart
Step 8). Open one real span document, compare, and adjust the patterns before trusting any alarm.

Assumed span document shape (CloudWatch Transaction Search): top-level `name`, `traceId`,
`durationNano`, `status.code`, and `attributes.<key>` for span attributes (flat keys such as
`attributes.compliance_status` need no quoting; dotted OpenTelemetry keys such as
`attributes."gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"` do).

Log group: `aws/spans`. Namespace for the metrics below: `ConvAI/WealthAgent`.

## Metric filters

Create each on the `aws/spans` log group (`aws logs put-metric-filter`).

| Metric | Filter pattern | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `AgentTurns` | `{ $.name = "wealth_agent.turn" }` | 1 |
| `AgentErrors` | `{ $.name = "wealth_agent.turn" && $.status.code = "ERROR" }` | 1 |
| `ToolCalls` | `{ $.name = "execute_tool*" }` | 1 |
| `ToolErrors` | `{ $.name = "execute_tool*" && $.attributes.tool_ok IS FALSE }` | 1 |
| `GuardrailFailures` | `{ $.name = "wealth_agent.turn" && $.attributes.compliance_status = "fail" }` | 1 |
| `TurnDurationNano` | `{ $.name = "wealth_agent.turn" }` | `$.durationNano` |

Example:

```bash
aws logs put-metric-filter --region <region> --log-group-name aws/spans \
  --filter-name convai-agent-errors \
  --filter-pattern '{ $.name = "wealth_agent.turn" && $.status.code = "ERROR" }' \
  --metric-transformations metricName=AgentErrors,metricNamespace=ConvAI/WealthAgent,metricValue=1,defaultValue=0
```

Notes:

- A failed guardrail is a policy outcome, not an error: the turn span status stays `OK`, so
  `AgentErrors` counts only unexpected exceptions.
- `GuardrailFailures` counts **turns** with any failed check, including a missing disclaimer. With a
  small local model this will be frequent; review the threshold after the first AWS run.
- Tool failures also appear in `GuardrailFailures` (the tool check is part of the compliance roll-up).

## p95 latency

Logs metric filters cannot compute percentiles. Options, in order of preference:

1. **CloudWatch Application Signals** (if enabled): alarm on its `Latency` p95 for the
   `convai-wealth-agent` service (`alarms.json`, `convai-wealth-agent-p95-latency`). Confirm the
   metric dimensions in the console.
2. **Fallback, a POC approximation**: alarm on the average of `TurnDurationNano`, threshold
   `8000000000` (8 s), statistic `Average`, period 300 s. An average hides slow outliers, so mark the
   alarm description as an approximation.

The dashboard's latency widget uses Logs Insights `pct()` and does not depend on either option.

## Logs Insights queries

Used by `dashboard.json`; run them against `aws/spans`.

```text
# Turns per minute
filter name = 'wealth_agent.turn' | stats count() by bin(1m)

# Latency percentiles (seconds)
filter name = 'wealth_agent.turn'
| stats pct(durationNano/1000000000, 50) as p50, pct(durationNano/1000000000, 95) as p95 by bin(5m)

# Failed turns and why
filter name = 'wealth_agent.turn' and attributes.compliance_status = 'fail'
| fields @timestamp, attributes.`session.id`, attributes.compliance_failed_rules, traceId
| sort @timestamp desc | limit 50

# Tool failures by tool
filter name like /^execute_tool/ and attributes.tool_ok = 0
| stats count() by attributes.`gen_ai.tool.name`

# Token usage
filter name = 'chat'
| stats sum(attributes.`gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`), sum(attributes.`gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`) by bin(5m)
```

Token usage is present only when the model reports it (Ollama usually does; verify).
